title: Croft
description: Deploy and host the apps your AI assistant builds — a real server, database, and shareable URL.
summary: Deploy and host the apps your AI assistant builds — a real server, database, and shareable URL.
offersHint: Deploy and host the apps your AI assistant builds — a real server, database, and shareable URL. · Remote MCP (streamable-http) at https://mcp.oncroft.net

toolsPreview.name: get_platform_conventions
toolsPreview.description: Return the Croft golden-path rules that every app on this workspace must follow.

toolsPreview.name: list_apps
toolsPreview.description: List the apps in this workspace with their URLs, status, and last release.

toolsPreview.name: create_app
toolsPreview.description: Provisions an empty app on this workspace: a git repo, subdomain, port, and golden-path scaffold files. It contains no feature implementation and is not yet live.

toolsPreview.name: get_app
toolsPreview.description: Get an app's file manifest, recent releases, and secret key names.

toolsPreview.name: read_file
toolsPreview.description: Read one file from an app's own git repo on this Croft workspace. No external API — the path is resolved inside the app's repository.

toolsPreview.name: write_files
toolsPreview.description: Writes files into an app's git repo and commits them (as 'Claude via Croft'). files is a list of {path, content}. Committed files are staged in the repo; they are not built or published until the app is deployed.

toolsPreview.name: deploy
toolsPreview.description: Commits, builds (Nixpacks), and deploys the app. Returns a deploy job id; the build runs in the background and its deploy_state moves through queued and running before it ends in succeeded or failed. The app is live only once the deploy has succeeded.

toolsPreview.name: status
toolsPreview.description: Reports an app's deploy and health status. `live` is true only when the latest deploy has fully succeeded; `deploy_state` gives the current stage (queued, running, succeeded, or failed). Read-only and safe to call repeatedly — each call returns the current stage, so it can be polled to follow a deploy's progress.

toolsPreview.name: logs
toolsPreview.description: Recent runtime logs for an app (relayed from its box).

toolsPreview.name: rollback
toolsPreview.description: Re-deploy the previous release of an app.

toolsPreview.name: delete_app
toolsPreview.description: Permanently deletes an app: removes its containers, data, and source code from the server, then deletes the app record. Irreversible. Does not affect other apps or the server. Deletes only when confirm is true.

toolsPreview.name: set_secret
toolsPreview.description: Set (or replace) an env secret for an app. Value is stored encrypted and injected at deploy.

toolsPreview.name: list_secret_keys
toolsPreview.description: List an app's secret key names (never values).

toolsPreview.name: list_users
toolsPreview.description: List the people in this workspace and which apps they can access.

toolsPreview.name: invite_user
toolsPreview.description: Invite someone by email, set their workspace role, and grant app access. role is member (use apps), creator (can build their own apps), or admin. apps is 'all' or a list of app names.

toolsPreview.name: grant_access
toolsPreview.description: Grant an existing user access to an app.

toolsPreview.name: revoke_access
toolsPreview.description: Revoke a user's access to an app.

toolsPreview.name: set_public_paths
toolsPreview.description: Sets which of an app's paths are reachable WITHOUT login. By default an app is fully private (workspace login required everywhere). Pass the complete desired list of specific paths (e.g. ["/survey"]); each listed path and everything under it becomes public, everything else stays private. An empty list makes the app fully private again. The whole app cannot be made public — root or wildcard paths are rejected.

toolsPreview.name: set_schedules
toolsPreview.description: Sets the app's scheduled tasks. Each is { name, cron, path }: on the cron (standard 5-field, UTC) Croft makes an internal POST to the app's path, and the app does the work (e.g. send a daily email, sync an API). Use this for anything recurring instead of writing your own cron — it survives deploys and reboots and is shown in the panel. Also implement the endpoint (e.g. a POST route at that path). Pass the full desired list; an empty list clears all schedules.

toolsPreview.name: set_database_sharing
toolsPreview.description: Turns this app's database sharing on or off. Off by default (the database is private). When on, other apps in the same workspace may read AND write this app's SQLite database through Croft's internal broker at http://croft-data:8080/q/<this-app-name> (send {"sql":"…","params":[…]}), and this app is listed to other apps as reusable shared data. Turn it on for an app whose data other apps should reuse — e.g. a CRM's contacts list that an invoicing app also needs.

toolsPreview.name: list_connectors
toolsPreview.description: Lists the workspace's API connectors (external services apps can call without holding the credential) and their state. `active` connectors are usable; `draft` ones still need a workspace admin to add the credential.

toolsPreview.name: describe_connector
toolsPreview.description: Returns a connector's full manifest — base URL, auth style, and the named operations (method, path, params) an app can call. Never returns the credential.

toolsPreview.name: propose_connector
toolsPreview.description: Creates a new API connector as a DRAFT from the vendor's API docs: you supply the base URL, auth style, and an operations manifest. A workspace member (owner, admin, or creator) then opens the panel and adds the credential to activate it — the credential never passes through you. auth_style is bearer|header|query|basic; for header/query also give auth_param (the header/param name).

toolsPreview.name: grant_connector
toolsPreview.description: Gives one of your apps access to a connector — no approval step. The app can then call the connector's operations. Note: this lets the app's code, and everyone the app is shared with, use the connector's credential. A connector an admin has marked admins-only can only be granted by an admin.

toolsPreview.name: list_grants
toolsPreview.description: Lists the connectors an app can reach and each grant's state.
